title: Smooth real manifold without boundary
statement: Over $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field], fix an integer $m\geq0$. A smooth $m$-manifold without boundary is a topological space $N$ with a covering atlas of homeomorphisms $x:U\to V$, where $U\subseteq N$ and $V\subseteq\mathbf R^m$ are open, such that every transition $y\circ x^{-1}$ is infinitely differentiable on its open domain. The model has no boundary or corners. Hausdorffness, second countability and compactness, when required, are additional hypotheses on $N$. Smooth scalar functions are functions whose expressions in these charts are infinitely differentiable.
